I-152-4.hang_root_cause: The 94-minute stall was a TEST-HARNESS artefact, not a product deadlock: the product-side pause hook pause_after_decision parks each racer on a two-party barrier before its transaction; after the two racers collided on the fems_workspace_write_anchors key (the guard working), the loser's bounded retry re-entered the closure and parked on the barrier a SECOND time while the winner had already left - a one-party wait on a cyclic two-party barrier, unbounded because the file had no bounds. Fix: the hook fires only on the first attempt (attempt counter in each closure: fems_memory.rs:81-92, 418-430, 524; workspaces.rs:11-22, 212-225; stage_artifacts.rs:36-47, 213-220, 375), so a retried attempt never touches the barrier and the interleaving cannot recur. items.title: title-anchor reclamation using the anchor row as the conflict key
items.detail: MT-142 rejected reclamation because a naive 'read live count then delete' reintroduces the R1-1-2 window. The safe design uses the MT-142 write-set discipline: every title-mutating transaction already UPSERTs the anchor row, so a reclamation transaction that DELETEs the anchor row writes the same key and collides at commit with any concurrent create/rename/delete on that title - one side loses, its bounded retry re-reads and either recreates the anchor (create path) or sees the new live document and skips (reclaim path). Implement reclamation inside the atomic delete transaction (knowledge.rs delete_knowledge_rich_document_atomic, around :2068 where the anchor is written): after tombstoning, LET $live = count of live documents in the workspace whose title_key equals the anchor's; IF $live = 0 THEN DELETE the anchor row. Also cover rename (the OLD title's anchor may become orphaned, same rule). Prove with a race test in both orders: delete-of-last-holder racing a create of the same title must end with exactly one anchor row and one live document, never zero anchors with a live document. Record the invariant in a doc comment: an anchor row exists for a title iff at least one live document holds it, eventually, with the transient window bounded by a single conflicting transaction.

items.title: migrate the eight remaining product-data locks onto the MT-142 primitives
items.detail: Static mutexes and acquisition sites: LOOM_MUTATION_LOCK (loom_store.rs:51, 15 sites via its guard helper), CANVAS_MUTATION_LOCK (loom_canvas_store.rs:51, 9), OVERLAY_MUTATION_LOCK / MARKDOWN_IMPORT_LOCK / WIKI_COMPILE_LOCK (wiki_store.rs:40-42, 4), BLOCK_VIEW_MUTATION_LOCK (block_view_store.rs:38, 2), BRIDGE_MUTATION_LOCK (bridge_store.rs:23, 1), DEPENDENCY_MUTATION_LOCK (locus_store.rs:37, 1). MT-151 proved every invariant behind them is now database-guarded (its audit table is in MT-151.json lifecycle.i_151_4_audit), so the mutexes are pure contention shaping. Replace each with the knowledge.rs pattern: the per-SurrealDatabase KeyedLockRegistry on the narrowest stable key (LockKey::Record for single-record mutations, NaturalKey for uniqueness/upsert races, Workspace only for invariants that genuinely span a workspace - the MT-142 contract's contention_control_requirements), wrapped in guarded_mutation-style bounded retry with pre-reads inside the closure. Delete the static mutexes (PT: zero occurrences of the ten names in src/). Prove: (a) every existing target that exercises those stores stays green (loom, canvas, wiki, block_view, bridge, locus targets - enumerate them from tests/ and run each once); (b) a new disjoint-record overlap proof per store family in the style of tests/surreal_swarm_semantics_tests.rs::disjoint_records_commit_concurrently_without_unrelated_waiting, asserting engine-window overlap >= 2 for two different Loom blocks, two Canvas boards and two Wiki projections; (c) a same-record race per family asserting one winner and typed losers.

items.title: memory envelope: measure, then bound if the engine allows it
items.detail: The RSS finding (413.9 MB and 433.99 MB of growth on an 18 MB store; 25x operations and 20x store for 1.9x growth against the CI profile) suggests fixed engine overhead. Two steps. MEASURE: run the extended load profile at constant worker count and buffer configuration while varying only operation_count (e.g. 5000, 20000, 50000 at 64 workers, same seed family) and record growth_bytes per run; state whether growth is ingest-proportional or fixed with the three points. BOUND: the research basis records RocksDB defaults of write_buffer_size 128 MiB x max_write_buffer_number 32 on machines with >= 64 GiB RAM (surrealdb-core-3.2.0 cnf.rs:31-50), i.e. up to 4 GiB of write buffers, and that the SDK never passes a ConfigMap. Read cnf.rs and the kvs/rocksdb config path in the pinned crates for ENVIRONMENT-driven knobs (historically SURREAL_ROCKSDB_* variables) and for anything reachable through the SDK's opt::Config or Capabilities; if a supported knob exists, expose it through SurrealStorageConfig with a documented default that bounds the engine's memory to a stated envelope, set it at open, and re-measure at the same workload to show the effect. If no supported knob exists, say so with the file:line evidence and record the envelope as a documented characteristic with the measured curve. Write a memory-envelope section into the manual page.
closes: RSS finding turned into a measured answer

items.title: FEMS_MUTATION_LOCK and STAGE_INSERT_LOCK under the caller-side statement bound
items.detail: Both take their mutex OUTSIDE with_data_operation, but a statement timeout still returns Err through them and drops the guard while the abandoned statement may be live. Audit every invariant each protects exactly as MT-151 I-151-4 did (table: site, invariant, database-side guard or LOCK-ONLY). Known: FEMS (src/storage/fems_memory.rs:1565, 7 sites) has CAS THROWs HSK-FEMS-REVIEW-STATE / COMMIT-STATE and create_if_absent for most invariants, but the D-146-1 workspace-delete ordering is lock-only by documented design - give it a database-side guard (an ordering anchor CAS like storage_graph_anchors, or a THROW on the ordering precondition inside the transaction) and prove it with a lock-registry-disabled race. STAGE (src/storage/stage_artifacts.rs:23, 1 site) is covered by uq_stage_capture_artifacts_idempotency - confirm and record. Then migrate both onto the keyed registry + bounded retry as in I-152-2 and delete the statics.
